A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The complete main text and Appendices A–F, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimizer and hybrid FO–ZO unlearning experiments on MUSE, WMDP-Bio and TOFU, alongside robustness, utility and ablation results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical studies, including the main experimental figures and supplementary results in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The gradient-compression methods, AdaZO configuration and alternating FO–ZO hybrid procedure remain unchanged, as do their objectives and update rules.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MUSE-Books, MUSE-News, WMDP-Bio, TOFU forget10 and the same utility benchmarks. Table A3's caption changes from MUSE-Books to MUSE-News, correcting the identification of existing results rather than adding dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within corresponding experiments. In particular, the revised panels in Figures 4(c) and A5(c) retain Adam, SAM, signAdam and Hybrid.

E3.justification: The models, training settings, metrics, quantization and relearning procedures in Sections 3–6 and Appendix D are unchanged. KnowMem was already evaluated in v1; the replacement plots do not establish a new protocol or experimental rerun.

E4.justification: The same mode-connectivity analyses, quantization and relearning tests, forget-versus-retain relearning analysis and switching-interval ablation remain. The replacement endpoint panels revise reporting within existing robustness analyses without adding or redesigning a test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 4(c) and A5(c) replace duplicated VerbMem panels with KnowMem results. Figure 4(c) now reports post-Relearn100 scores of 46.0 for Adam and 34.4 for Hybrid; these are newly displayed metric results, not performance gains between versions. In v4, A5(c)'s Adam/signAdam scores of 46.0/45.0 disagree with the retained A3(c) scores of 58.6/49.2 under the same stated MUSE-News setting. Table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), the optimizer-grade and mode-connectivity definitions, and the randomized-smoothing reasoning are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims linking optimizer downgrading to robustness and proposing FO–ZO hybrid optimization for effective, resilient unlearning.

C2.justification: The noise-tolerance, optimization-basin and leader–follower explanations are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same limitations concerning omitted optimizers and untested applications; no explanation is added for the revised plots.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code destination from OPTML-Group/Unlearn_Optim to OPTML-Group/Unlearn_Optimizer, including the hyperlink target. Both versions still say code will be available, so the PDFs do not establish a release or improved accessibility. Implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged, including positioning against objective-based robustness defenses and earlier zeroth-order optimization research.

P1.justification: The MIT-IBM affiliation superscript is corrected from 1 to 2. Section 8 adds Schmidt Sciences and CAIS award acknowledgements and removes the MIT-IBM thanks. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 4(c) and A5(c) each replace a duplicated VerbMem plot with a KnowMem bar chart, changing the corresponding axis label and scale. Table A3's dataset caption is corrected to MUSE-News. The remaining displays and their placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table A3's caption and replacing duplicated plots improves identification and completeness of the reported evidence. However, the new Figure A5(c) disagrees with retained Figure A3(c): Adam/signAdam KnowMem scores after 100 relearning steps are 46.0/45.0 versus 58.6/49.2 for the same stated MUSE-News setting. Without an explanation or documented setting difference, the reliability of this added evidence remains unresolved, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
